## What this is

A bot that watches your ESPN fantasy league.

It talks in Discord. It also keeps a website of the season.

You do not start it on game day. It is already running.

::: {.notes}
The container stays up all season. League members only need Discord and a browser. No one has to remember a schedule or log into ESPN to see the same numbers.
:::

## Three things you get

::: {.trio}
::: {#post}

::: {.num}
Channel
:::

### Scheduled posts

Scoreboards, matchups, standings, and trophies land in Discord on their own.

:::

::: {#ask}

::: {.num}
Anytime
:::

### Slash commands

Type a command in the server when you want the current week, not the last post.

:::

::: {#see}

::: {.num}
The season
:::

### Web dashboard

Charts, records, and season awards from every week the bot has saved.

:::
:::

::: {.notes}
These are the only three surfaces. Scheduled posts use a webhook. Slash commands need the bot invited to the server. The dashboard is a web page, local or on a public URL.
:::

## What shows up in Discord

Each post is one report. Typical reports:

- Current scores and projections
- Close games
- Final scores and weekly trophies
- Power rankings and standings
- Thursday matchups
- Waiver moves
- Sunday injury watch

::: {.notes}
The tone matches ESPN's own reports: names, scores, ranks. Private leagues need ESPN cookies before waiver moves appear. Public leagues skip that report.
:::

::: {.notes}
Tuesday morning also saves the finished week to the dashboard database. That is why the website trails live Discord by a day: it waits until Monday night football is over.
:::

## Ask the bot yourself

Type `/` in Discord. Pick a command:

::: {.cmds}
- `/matchups` <span>this week's games</span>
- `/scoreboard` <span>live scores</span>
- `/standings` <span>the table</span>
- `/power-rankings` <span>who is hot</span>
- `/monitor` <span>injuries</span>
- `/trophies` <span>this week's awards</span>
- `/waiver-report` <span>adds and drops</span>
- `/dashboard` <span>link to the site</span>
:::

::: {.notes}
Commands read ESPN live. The dashboard reads the saved season. If they disagree on year, the dashboard is behind until the next Tuesday snapshot, or until someone backfills a prior season.
:::

## The dashboard

A dark page of the whole season, not only this week.

- Filter weeks: regular season, playoffs, or a custom range
- Pick a season if more than one is saved
- Click a team. Every chart follows that team
- Click a trophy. You jump to that week on the trend chart

The page refreshes itself about every 30 seconds.

::: {.notes}
Empty dashboard means no snapshot has run yet. A completed past season can be loaded with the backfill script. League members never need that command; it is a maintainer step.
:::

## Five views

::: {.tabs}
::: {.tab}
### Trend

How each team scored, week by week. Cumulative, rank, or versus projection.
:::

::: {.tab}
### Standings

Wins, point differential, streak, and recent form.
:::

::: {.tab}
### Spread

Who is steady and who swings. Median, floor, ceiling.
:::

::: {.tab}
### Head to head

Every pairing, tinted by typical margin.
:::

::: {.tab}
### Trophies

Eleven season awards. Click one to jump to that week.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Trophies is the fifth tab. It did not fit the four-up grid. Cover it on the next slide. Eleven awards: highest and lowest score, closest game, biggest blowout, luckiest win, unluckiest loss, streak, points against, best and worst versus projection, biggest week-to-week swing.
:::

## Season trophies

Eleven awards, not a single champion graphic.

Highest score. Closest game. Biggest blowout. Luckiest win.

Click an award. The dashboard focuses that team and marks the week.

::: {.notes}
This is the feature people remember. The old version showed the award and stopped. Now the card is a way into the chart.
:::

## What you do

Nothing on Sunday morning.

Open Discord for the latest post, or type a slash command.

Open the dashboard when you want the season, not the week.

::: {.notes}
If someone asks how to log in: they don't. Discord is the league server they already belong to. The dashboard is a public URL if the tunnel is up, or localhost:8000 on the host machine.
:::
